item.title: Twisted TV: How a Documentary Bent the Facts Out of Shape. 1. MISA in Romania
item.description: An Apple TV series against Gregorian Bivolaru and his movement even rehabilitates the notorious Securitate police of Ceaușescu.

item.title: China’s New “Illegal Activity”: Providing Legal Defense to Christians
item.description: Lawyers for Zion Church face suspensions, threats, and pressure to renounce both their cases and their faith.

item.title: Twisted TV: How a Documentary Bent the Facts Out of Shape. 2. Enter Hugues Gascan
item.description: The strange but important role of a shadowy figure in instigating the prosecution of Bivolaru and MISA in France.

item.title: China’s New Retirement Plan for Dissidents: Work, Prison, Repay, Repeat
item.description: New research shows how authorities have found a new way to punish prisoners of conscience by taking away their earned pensions.

item.title: Twisted TV: How a Documentary Bent the Facts Out of Shape. 3. The “Victims”
item.description: “Apostate” ex-members have a right to express their distress, and their stories should be carefully considered. But are they always believable?

item.title: The New Law on Ethnic Unity: A Threat to Tibetan Buddhism
item.description: The new policy assaults the Tibetan language and thus Tibet’s cultural and religious foundations.

item.title: The Tokyo High Court Unification Church Decision. 4. The 2009 “Compliance Declaration”
item.description: After 2009, the number of incidents involving alleged improper solicitation of donations dropped to nearly zero. But the court maintains the problem still exists.

item.title: Tai Ji Men, Human Dignity, and the Natural Law
item.description: Defending victims of injustice is not only an act of solidarity but a basic requirement of natural law. This is the lesson the Tai Ji Men case brings to mind.

item.title: China Hails Japan’s Dissolution of the Unification Church
item.description: The Chinese Communist Party celebrates Japan’s court ruling as a welcome boost to its global campaign against an unwelcome church.

item.title: Women’s History Month Must Not Forget Uyghur Women
item.description: Detention in mass camps, forced sterilization, coerced birth control, and sexual abuse are rarely mentioned. Perhaps economic ties with China make criticism inconvenient.

item.title: The Tokyo High Court Unification Church Decision. 5. Violating International Law
item.description: Restricting freedom of religion or belief on the grounds of “social acceptability” and “public welfare” is prohibited by the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights.

item.title: The Tokyo High Court Unification Church Decision. 6. Who Will Protect the Believers?
item.description: The court assures us that individual devotees will not be discriminated against. The reality is different.

item.title: 統一教会に対する東京高裁の決定 2. 洗脳論の亡霊
item.description: 本決定の重要なテーマの一つは、「カルト」が「精神操作」によってその信者を騙すという、すでに否定された疑似科学的理論である。

item.title: A Human Rights Crisis in Taiwan: The Tai Ji Men Case
item.description: An international webinar compared what happened to Tai Ji Men with other cases of gross human rights violations.

item.title: China’s Battle for the Dead: Guangdong Villagers Oppose Crematorium Project, Clash with Police
item.description: Residents of Shuikou Town protest for days as authorities deploy riot police and tighten control. It is another chapter in a “war” about burial practices in rural China.
